source: បច្ចេកទេស ដាំដុះដំណាំដំឡូងជ្វា (Sweet Potato Cultivation Techniques), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, 2018
text:
In Cambodia, farmers in many provinces grow sweet potato (ដំឡូងជ្វា), a root/tuber crop that has long been cultivated by generations of farmers, with cultivated area gradually increasing across the country.

Sweet potato tubers form underground and contain abundant starch, providing good nutritional benefit. Approximately 100 grams of fresh sweet potato tuber provides about 25 grams of starch and roughly 50 kilocalories of energy. Beyond starch, the tuber also contains vitamins and minerals, with only a small amount of fat. Because of its high, good-quality carbohydrate content, sweet potato is considered a beneficial food for consumers, and has traditionally served as a supplementary staple food, particularly valuable during times of rice scarcity because it is easy to grow and multiply.

Analysis of the tuber's composition shows it contains approximately 24% pure starch and 4.17% glucose while fresh, and when ground into flour, approximately 1.3% protein, 4.24% tannin, and 1.37% pentosan, along with vitamins A, B, and C.
